name: 2025-26 Makeup - CSE_2123-DIGITAL SYSTEM DESIGN
subject: Digital System Design

questions.markdown: Design a sequential circuit with two JK flip-flops $A$ and $B$ and two inputs $E$ and $F$. If $E = 0$, the circuit remains in the same state regardless of the value of $F$. When $E = 1$ and $F = 1$, the circuit goes through the state transitions from $00$ to $01$, to $10$, to $11$, back to $00$, and repeats. When $E = 1$ and $F = 0$, the circuit goes through the state transitions from $00$ to $11$, to $10$, to $01$, back to $00$, and repeats.

Show the transistor-level diagram for a two-input CMOS NAND gate. Determine why the NMOS transistors are placed in series in the pull-down network, while the PMOS transistors are placed in parallel in the pull-up network to achieve the NAND logic function.
Simplify the function $F(a,b,c,d) = \Pi M(1,3,5,8,9,11,15) + D(2,13)$ using K-map to obtain the minimum cost SOP expression and draw the circuit.

Apply the concept of the Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) by deriving the general expressions for the Carry Generate $(G_i)$, Carry Propagate $(P_i)$, and the output carry $(C_{i+1})$ for a single stage. Apply these concepts to write the specific logical expressions for the output carries $C_1$ and $C_2$ in terms of the initial carry $C_0$ and the corresponding $G$ and $P$ terms. Explain why the CLA is faster than a Ripple Carry Adder.
Design a 4-to-1 multiplexer using only 2-to-1 multiplexers. Implement this design in Verilog HDL and simulate the circuit.

questions.markdown: Apply the necessary external logic connections to a JK Flip-Flop to convert it into an equivalent T Flip-Flop. Explain the simple modification required on the J and K inputs to achieve the toggle function when needed.
Apply the understanding of sequential circuits to design a basic RS latch using NOR gates. Demonstrate its working with a detailed circuit diagram and truth table.
Construct an ASM chart for the pseudo code of a bit counter and explain it.

Determine the operation of a Serial-In, Parallel-Out (SIPO) Shift Register. Explain the specific steps (in terms of clock cycles) required to load an 8-bit data word into the register and how the data is then accessed at the output terminals.
Apply the design principles of an Asynchronous (Ripple) Counter and the operational constraints of a Positive Edge-Triggered T Flip-Flop to implement a 4-bit UP counter in Verilog.

Draw the standard symbol and the truth table for a Tri-state Driver. Apply the Tri-state Driver to explain how the outputs of two registers $R1$ and $R2$ are safely connected to a common bus line with the help of a diagram.
Design a three-bit counter that counts in the sequence $0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 0$.
Show the relationship between the number of states $N$ generated by a simple ring counter and the number of flip-flops $k$ used.
